per_policy_guidance.guidance: Observed reliability: 7/12 (58.3%) from this policy’s own demonstrated segment-entry states, under the 1,425-step budget. Use only with valid lid pose, a closed/partly open lid, stationary in-box peg, and a reachable, collision-free handle approach. Its moving-lid body-frame prior is intended for direct contact geometry when assembly displacement/reorientation is the selector concern, but that benefit has no out-of-distribution validation. Avoid as the nominal first choice given five validation failures; also avoid after release if lid motion would drag the moving reference, with unreliable lid pose, or when IK/reachability is poor. Recognize failure from closure without synchronized lid motion, stalled/reversing opening, growing TCP-to-handle error, peg motion, repeated IK/limit issues, or failure of the TCP to clear after release. Two failed runs briefly met the exit rule and then finished nearly closed, and another finished at 1.005 rad without satisfying the full exit, so do not hand off on a transient angle crossing or angle alone. Continue through release/retreat until physical observations persistently show cover >0.9 rad, open fingers, TCP >0.10 m from the handle and clear of the panel, low lid velocity, and peg displacement <1 cm. Then hand off to retrieve_peg_from_box; preserve both causal frames. The supervised [740,950) overlap supports a later handoff after settling. If release/settling is the uncertainty near nominal placement, prefer h03; if the TCP/joints are off the nominal path but local geometry is valid, prefer h02.

Observed reliability: 12/12 (100%) from this policy’s own demonstrated segment-entry states. It first met the exit rule at steps 689–863; final cover angles were 1.337–1.666 rad and peg motion remained only about 2.7–3.6e-6 m. This is a primary in-distribution choice. Its fresh-TCP incremental prior is intended for a collision-free replan, partly open lid, or unusual TCP/joint entry when handle-relative geometry remains plausible and corrections are locally reachable; those off-path benefits are design intent, not out-of-distribution evidence. Avoid when handle/lid geometry is unreliable, corrections are unreachable/blocked, contact has already been lost, or local commands shrink, accumulate bias, or oscillate. Recognize failure from ineffective incremental motion, orientation oscillation, closure away from the handle, lack of synchronized lid motion, stalled/reversing angle, or peg motion. Every successful validation run contained some IK-unconverged steps (11–129), so nonzero counts alone did not imply failure; use repeated/growing residuals or limit contacts together with lack of physical progress as the stop/switch cue. Hand off to retrieve_peg_from_box only after observed open fingers, cover >0.9 rad and stable with low velocity, TCP >0.10 m from the handle and clear of the panel, and peg displacement <1 cm. Preserve the two causal observations across the switch; the full [740,950) pull/release/retreat overlap permits waiting for clearance. Prefer h04/h01 if installation-frame displacement is the dominant concern, or h03 when nominal release-phase ambiguity dominates.

Observed reliability: 10/12 (83.3%) from this policy’s own demonstrated segment-entry states. Successful runs first met the exit rule at steps 585–1,355, so allow ample budget and verify completion physically. Use near the demonstrated installation when close-versus-pull, maximum-opening-versus-release, or release-versus-retreat phase ambiguity is the main concern and the caller’s release angle is valid. The phase head is training support only, not a runtime success/contact signal. Avoid for large installation displacement, strongly off-path TCP/joint entries, arbitrary release angles, or states requiring missed-grasp/lost-contact recovery. Both failed validations ended with cover angle above 0.9 rad (1.401 and 1.042 rad) but never met the complete exit; each had only one gripper change and an open-command fraction of about 0.149. The data do not identify which remaining exit clause failed, so treat angle alone as insufficient and watch for premature opening, failure to release, mismatch between commanded and observed phase, lid reversal, large IK residuals after displacement, or peg motion. Hand off to retrieve_peg_from_box only from current physical observations: open fingers, stable cover >0.9 rad with low velocity, TCP >0.10 m from the handle and clear of the panel, and peg displacement <1 cm. Preserve both causal frames, and prefer later takeover while the released lid is moving. Prefer h02 for off-path robot entry and h04/h01 when installation displacement is the selector concern; none of those out-of-distribution cases was validated.

Observed reliability: 12/12 (100%) from this policy’s own demonstrated segment-entry states. It first met the exit rule at steps 496–907; every final cover angle was about 1.85 rad, final peg motion was about 2.7–3.6e-6 m, and validation reported zero IK-unconverged steps. This is a primary in-distribution choice when lid_pose and lid_position coherently describe the same one-axis hinge, the peg is stationary, and the stationary-root transformed path is reachable and collision-free. Its hinge-canonical frame and separate open/close scores are intended to handle rigid installation transforms and sparse release timing, but displaced installations were not validated. Avoid or switch if pose/angle/axis disagree, the reconstructed root or target drifts with lid angle, the TCP/joints are strongly off the canonical path, or transformed targets are blocked/unreachable. Recognize failure from growing TCP-to-handle error, closure without synchronized lid motion, stalled/reversing angle, early opening or fingers staying closed after maximum opening, repeated IK/limit problems, failure to clear the panel, or peg motion. Learned mode scores and the caller release angle are not completion evidence. Continue through release and retreat until observed fingers are open, cover >0.9 rad and stable with low velocity, TCP is >0.10 m from the handle and clear of the moving panel, and peg displacement is <1 cm. Then hand off to retrieve_peg_from_box while preserving both causal frames; the [740,950) supervised overlap supports waiting through settling. Prefer h02 for a strongly off-path TCP/arm entry; h03 is the near-nominal world/phase alternative and h01 the direct moving-body alternative.

summary: Validation is strictly in distribution: each policy was run from the entry state of its own training segment in each of 12 demonstrations, with training call arguments and a 1.5× segment budget. There is no evidence for displaced installations, unusual robot entries, missed/lost-contact recovery, collisions, or other out-of-distribution conditions; the priors only indicate which policy was designed for those situations. In-distribution results rank h02 and h04 jointly highest at 12/12, followed by h03 at 10/12 and h01 at 7/12. If the input geometry is coherent and otherwise nominal, h04 and h02 are the primary choices: select h04 for its stationary hinge-canonical representation and h02 for fresh-TCP local correction. Validation alone does not prove either superior overall; h04 had zero reported IK-unconverged steps and final angles near 1.85 rad, while h02 also passed every run despite 11–129 IK-unconverged steps per run. Use h03 as a phase-focused near-nominal alternative, and h01 cautiously as the moving-lid-frame alternative because transient success later regressed in two failed runs. For every policy, completion and handoff must use the full physical exit rule—not lid angle, gripper command, auxiliary prediction, or mode score alone: cover >0.9 rad, observed release/open fingers, TCP >0.10 m from the handle and clear of the panel, stable/low lid velocity, and peg movement <1 cm. Hand off to retrieve_peg_from_box only after those observations hold, preferably after settling, and preserve the two-frame causal history across the switch.
